claude.sample_unit: patients (19 CHB-MIT, 22 Conegliano; 16 eligible for leave-out validation and calibration)

links.outcome: Performance under randomized cross-validation versus patient-independent leave-one-out testing
links.effect: Randomized CV gave very high performance that dropped dramatically under leave-one-patient-out testing; patient chb22 had best RCV accuracy (93.99%) but below-average LOO accuracy, suggesting RCV was biased by overfitting.
links.quote: As expected, the results show that RCV can lead to very high performance in terms of all evaluation metrics, but these numbers dramatically drop when the model is tested under the more realistic LOO validation condition.

links.outcome: Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity gains from fine-tuning CNN on one or two seizures of new patient
links.effect: CHB-MIT: Cal1 raised ACC/SEN/SPE by 12%/22%/14%, Cal2 by 16%/29%/16%. Conegliano: Cal1 15%/10%/16%, Cal2 23%/22%/30%. Repeated ANOVA p<0.001. Accuracy improved in all patients.
links.quote: Nevertheless, also with the Conegliano dataset after model calibration we obtain significant improvements in all metrics, with ACC, SEN and SPE gains of 15%, 10% and 16% for Cal1 and 23%, 22% and 30% for Cal2.

links.effect: Substantial heterogeneity across patients (e.g., p1 and p6 had very poor LOO accuracy; gains varied up to 25% in CHB-MIT and 47% in Conegliano); authors note non-negligible variability between patients.
links.quote: Furthermore, the non-negligible variability of forecasting accuracy between patients suggests that further efforts should be spent to improve the reliability of predictive models.

links.outcome: CNN versus XGBoost benchmark and calibration gains
links.effect: CNN outperformed traditional ML pipelines under RCV; calibration also helped XGBoost but with lower gains (ACC +6%/+10% CHB-MIT, +8%/+13% Conegliano) than CNN.
links.quote: It turns out that our calibration method is also effective with XGBoost, although the performance gains are slightly lower compared to the CNN.

unlisted_practices: Patient-specific fine-tuning of a pretrained seizure forecasting model using one or two recorded seizures
Leave-one-patient-out validation instead of randomized cross-validation

links.effect: For chb22, RCV accuracy was 93.99%; after LOO underperformance, one-seizure calibration accuracy was 79.84%, indicating RCV overfitting risk.
links.quote: For example, patient chb22 obtains the best accuracy among all patients in the RCV condition (93.99%) and, despite this number falling below the average accuracy in the LOO condition, it improves again to the best score after calibrating with just one seizure (79.84%).

links.outcome: Accuracy after one- or two-seizure calibration
links.effect: Across two datasets, deep-learning forecast accuracy increased on average by more than 20%, with performance improving systematically in all independent patients.
links.quote: We evaluate our calibration procedure using two datasets containing EEG signals recorded from a large cohort of epileptic subjects, demonstrating that the forecast accuracy of deep learning methods can increase on average by more than 20%, and that performance improves systematically in all independent patients.

links.outcome: overestimation of seizure forecasting performance from data leakage in randomized cross-validation
links.effect: Randomized cross-validation yielded high metrics that dropped dramatically under patient-independent leave-one-out validation; for example, patient chb22 accuracy fell from 93.99% under RCV to below average under LOO.
links.quote: As expected, the results show that RCV can lead to very high performance in terms of all evaluation metrics, but these numbers dramatically drop when the model is tested under the more realistic LOO validation condition.

unlisted_practices: Patient-specific model fine-tuning (calibration) using recorded seizure events from unseen patients

screen.reason: Evaluates the impact of a calibration/fine-tuning pipeline on independent patient EEG seizure forecasting compared to standard uncalibrated models across retrospective patient cohorts.
